text: Oh brilliant, the printer's decided today's the day. Right before the deadline. Love that for me.
Nothing says 'we value you' like a 6am email about mandatory fun on Saturday.
Fantastic news, the landlord's 'popping round' again. Can't wait to be told my own kitchen is dirty.
What a treat. Four hours in A&E with Gran, home at 3am, alarm at 6. I feel incredibly well rested, obviously.
Sure, Dad, tell me again how proud you'd have been if I'd stayed in law. Great chat. Lovely Sunday. Sat in the car for twenty minutes after.
Great. Another 'quick sync' that could have been a sentence. My afternoon thanks you.
Ah yes, the classic 'we've gone in a different direction' after three interviews and a presentation. So glad I ironed a shirt.
Wonderful, the train's cancelled, the interview's at nine and the next one is 'subject to availability'. Totally calm. Breathing into a paper bag, calmly.
Thanks so much, Ellis, for telling the whole table about my divorce. Really brought the mood up. Top work.
Because of course the one day I wear white, the one day. Soup. Obviously.
How lovely that the baby decided 3am was party time again. Really thriving over here. Living my best life.
Good to know my opinion was wanted so badly they made the decision before I got there. Very efficient.
'Just a few tweaks', he says. Fourteen pages of tweaks, the launch, the audit and the school play, all by Friday. Easy. I'll just stop sleeping.
Nothing like being asked 'so when are you two having kids' at a funeral. Really reading the room, Auntie Val.
Oh good, the app's updated and moved every button. Just what I wanted at 7am. Thank you, nameless designer.
Love that the gym's 'quiet hours' are the exact hours it's full of men grunting at themselves in the mirror.
Wow, a round of applause for me, I managed to get out of bed before noon. Somebody alert the press.
Cheers, body, for the migraine on the morning of Ana's wedding. Watched it on a video call from a dark room. Really the day I'd pictured.
Delighted to learn, via Facebook, that my brother got engaged. Family group chat clearly for emergencies only.
Perfect, the boiler's gone the first cold night of the year. Right on cue. Who needs hot water anyway.
Another day, another 'per my last email'. I'm so enriched by this correspondence.
Ten out of ten to Raj for cooking dinner and leaving every pan, again, after I asked him twice, in front of his mother. Teamwork makes the dream work. I'm livid.
So nice of the council to fix the pothole after two years, three bent wheels and Mr Ellis breaking his hip in it. Heroes. I'm writing to every one of them tonight.
Honestly, who needs sleep when you can have a neighbour who learns the drums at eleven at night.
Glad we spent the whole 'wellbeing day' in a windowless room being told to prioritise fresh air.
Cool, cool, cool. The hospital's lost the referral. Again. I'm sure the third time will be the charm.
Really appreciated Marta telling me I 'look tired'. I've been crying in the work toilets most mornings. So glad it shows.
A whole weekend of my own company. How thrilling. I might even talk to the fridge.
Fabulous. The 'unlimited holiday' policy that nobody's ever used without getting a Look. So generous.
Great job, me, forgetting the one thing I went to the shop for. Standing ovation. Encore.
Oh sure, let's all pretend the review was 'constructive'. Very constructive. I feel very built up.
What a joy to be the only one who remembered Mum's birthday. My siblings are truly a gift.
Yeah, no, I'm totally fine with everyone else getting the bonus. Totally. Fine. Love it here.
Nice one, weather. Forecast said sun. I've been at the beach in a cagoule since nine like an idiot.
Thrilled to see my ex is 'living her best life' in Bali. Truly. Scrolling with great serenity.
Such a privilege to be CC'd on forty emails about a team night out I'm apparently not invited to. Really feel part of something.
Of course the one night I go to bed early is the night the fire alarm goes off at 2am for burnt toast. Naturally.
Oh, the IT team 'can't replicate the issue'. Amazing. It only replicates itself every single hour on my screen.
Good to know Karl thinks I 'got lucky' with the deal. Six months of work. Very lucky. Should play the lottery.
Marvellous, the baby monitor's picking up next door's radio. Nothing soothes a 4am feed like phone-in talk about parking.
Love that I'm the 'organised one', which apparently means I'm organising Mum's move, the reunion and the school fair at once. What an honour. I can't see the edges of it.
Fantastic, another Friday night swiping through people whose first message is 'hey'. The romance of the age. Just me, the cat and the glow of the screen.
Oh great, the GP's booking line opens at 8am, the appointments are gone by 8:01, and the lump is still there. Such a well-oiled machine. Totally fine. Not thinking about it at all.
How kind of the universe to put the parking fine, the dentist bill and the rent rise in the same post, with £43 in the account. Really spoiling me. Lying awake doing sums for fun.
Yes, Nadia, I'm sure your two-year-old's sleep schedule is exactly what my dissertation needed to hear about for an hour.
Brilliant, a 'surprise' audit on the day Leo's off, with the month-end close and two new starters to train. Living the dream. Don't know where to start, so I'm staring at the inbox.
Lovely to spend my birthday answering emails from people who don't know it's my birthday. Festive.
Well done to whoever decided the office should be nineteen degrees in December. Toasty. Can almost feel my hands.
Oh no, the client wants it 'more pop but also more muted'. Absolutely. I'll get right on that paradox.
So glad I rushed across town for the 'quick catch-up' with Imogen, the first in a year, and she cancelled by text while I was on the bus. Time well spent. Ate the cake I'd bought on a bench.
Cheers to the bank for freezing my card for 'unusual activity'. The unusual activity was buying lunch.
What a thrill, the heating engineer's window is 8am to 6pm on the one day off I've had in three weeks. Sat on the stairs all day too exhausted to even nap. Cosy.
Great chat with Mum where she asked if I'm 'still doing the little art thing'. Fifteen years. The little art thing.
Yes, let's definitely have the team-building at a climbing wall the week after I said I'm scared of heights. Inspired. My stomach's been in knots since the calendar invite.
Smashing. Woke up at five to a flat tyre, a dead phone and a cat sick on the stairs, after four hours' sleep. The trilogy. I can barely keep my eyes open and it's not even nine.
Honestly can't thank Sven enough for 'fixing' the shelf so it now falls on a timer.
Wonderful. My tax code's changed again for reasons known only to a computer in Newcastle. Love a mystery.
Ah, the family WhatsApp has decided I should 'come home more'. From the people who've visited me zero times in six years. Noted.
What a time to be alive: my coffee machine needs a firmware update before it will make coffee.
Super. Three missed calls from the school and now voicemail's 'full'. Can't imagine what's happened. Very relaxed.
Oh no. Disaster. The meeting's cancelled and I have to spend the afternoon in the garden with a book. However will I cope.
Terrible news: Bilal booked the whole week off for us and hid the passports so I can't back out. The cheek of it. Can't stop grinning.
Absolutely awful. My sister turned up with a casserole, did my washing up and refused to let me thank her. Some people, honestly.
Ugh, the worst. The physio says I'm 'ahead of schedule' and I have to stop using the stick. My poor stick. It had a good run.
Shocking behaviour from the kids this morning: breakfast in bed, a card with my name spelt wrong and a dance routine at seven. Who raised them. Oh wait.
Awful day. Ran the whole 5k without stopping for the first time and now I have to buy proper trainers like some sort of runner. The horror.
Very upsetting: nothing to do this Sunday. No plans, no visitors, just tea and the crossword. I may never recover.
Tragic news: the landlord's selling, so we finally have to buy that little flat by the canal we've been eyeing for three years. Woe is us. Viewing's on Saturday.
Oh great, Mum's got the all-clear and now she won't stop talking about her cruise. Twenty minutes on deck chairs. Unbearable. Honestly so relieved I could cry.
How dare Kofi remember the café where we met ten years ago and book a table there without telling me. Outrageous. I've been smiling at my soup.
Disaster: the presentation went so well they want me to lead the whole project. More work. Poor me. Did a little dance in the lift.
Dreadful weekend of doing absolutely nothing useful. Slept nine hours, walked by the sea, read on the sofa. Shameful. Would do again.
